critical_code_review_comments: CRITICAL (fixed): 6 frontend files (AuthContext.jsx, Chatbot.jsx, Dashboard.jsx, IndianQuiz.jsx, Leaderboard.jsx, WorldExplorer.jsx) shipped with broken imports — literal `__PLACE__` token replaced `from "@/lib/api";` AND `devWarn` was NEVER added to the import list, so every file referenced an undefined identifier. Production build failed with 6× 'Syntax error: Unexpected token, expected "from"'. Root cause: the sweep-replace regex used to change `console.warn(` → `devWarn(` (or a companion edit that was meant to update the import) went wrong and rewrote the `from …` clause into a literal placeholder. Fix applied: replaced each broken import with `import { …existing…, devWarn } from "@/lib/api";`.

WeatherBackground.jsx (line 1) DID have the correct `import { devWarn } from "@/lib/api";` — so the broken sweep only hit files that were re-importing multiple items from api.js. Worth reviewing your sweep-script to understand why single-item imports survived but multi-item ones didn't.

rca_of_the_issue: Sweep-replace of `console.warn(` → `devWarn(` (or a paired 'add devWarn to imports' edit) went sideways. The regex ate everything from the closing `}` of the destructured import through the semicolon and replaced it with a literal `__PLACE__` string — presumably a placeholder token meant to be filled in by a follow-up step that never ran. Additionally, the edit failed to add `devWarn` to the destructured import list. Reproduction: `git show` on the pre-refactor files would show `import { api } from "@/lib/api";` and post-refactor shows `import { api } __PLACE__` (with `devWarn(` calls in the file body — all referencing an undefined identifier). Mitigation applied: replaced each `__PLACE__` marker with `, devWarn } from "@/lib/api";` (folding devWarn into the existing destructured import list). All 6 files rebuilt clean, verified via `yarn build` + browser regression sweep.
